title: All code should be reachable
description: Unreachable code is code that can never be executed. This usually happens when there is a return, break, continue, or raise statement before the code, or when a condition is always false. Unreachable code is dead code: it increases maintenance costs, can hide bugs, and makes the codebase harder to understand.
message: Unreachable code detected. This code will never be executed.

impact.reliability: Medium impact on code maintainability and potential for hidden bugs
impact.maintainability: High impact on code clarity and maintenance effort

recommendation: Remove unreachable code or restructure the logic to make the code reachable if it serves a purpose.

references.title: Python PEP 8 - Style Guide for Python Code

noncompliant.code:
if False:
    print("This will never execute")  # Unreachable code

why_is_this_an_issue: Unreachable code creates several problems: (1) It increases the codebase size without providing any functionality, (2) It can confuse developers who might think the code serves a purpose, (3) It can hide bugs or logic errors in the surrounding code, (4) It makes code reviews more difficult as reviewers need to identify dead code, (5) It can lead to false assumptions about code behavior during debugging.

how_to_fix.description: Identify unreachable code blocks after return, break, continue, or raise statements
Determine if the unreachable code was intended to execute under certain conditions
If the code is truly unnecessary, remove it completely
If the code should execute, restructure the control flow (move statements before return/break/continue)
For conditional unreachable code, review the conditions to ensure they can evaluate to true when needed
Run tests to ensure removing or restructuring doesn't break functionality
